headline: Colorado Golf Course Transforms Rough Into Thriving Wildlife Habitat
meta_description: A Colorado golf course is converting its rough into native wildflower habitat, attracting 40 bird species and boosting pollinator populations.
summary_short: A Colorado golf course is turning its rough into wildlife habitat. Native wildflowers are already bringing more bees and pollinators to the 337-acre property.
body:
A Colorado golf course is converting its rough into native wildflower habitat, with early results already showing promise for local wildlife. Native wildflowers planted across the property are attracting increased populations of bees and other pollinators, transforming what was once manicured turf into a thriving ecological space.

Birders recently counted around 40 bird species across the 337-acre course, a sign that the habitat shift is working. The initiative demonstrates how recreational spaces can be redesigned to support biodiversity without sacrificing their original purpose. By allowing native plants to flourish in areas typically kept short, the golf course has created new food sources and shelter for wildlife.
